# Houselights decision packet
Fresh research with live Qloo calls. Generated 2026-10-24T07:42:31.705Z. Decision support only: nothing has been booked, offered or approved.

## 1. Event brief
- Market: New York
- Audience reference artists (Qloo anchors): Leon Bridges
- 2 slots · $14,500 artist budget · max 2 per genre · 8 candidates

## 2. Recommendation (for human approval)
**Michael Kiwanuka + Sault** — $13,500 planned artist fees, $1,000 unallocated, 68.68 policy points.
Recommended: it maximizes the declared cultural-fit objective and continues in 27/27 disruption scenarios.
- **Michael Kiwanuka** · $6,500 (Illustrative demo value; availability: Illustrative demo value)
  - Ranks 1 of 8 candidates against Leon Bridges in New York. Relative order, not demand. [r9]
  - Qloo returned geographic popularity rows within New York. [a2]
  - An aggregate audience comparison with the anchors was returned. It does not measure shared ticket buyers. [a3]
- **Sault** · $7,000 (Illustrative demo value; availability: Illustrative demo value)
  - Ranks 5 of 8 candidates against Leon Bridges in New York. Relative order, not demand. [r9]
  - Qloo returned geographic popularity rows within New York. [r17]
  - An aggregate audience comparison with the anchors was returned. It does not measure shared ticket buyers. [r18]

## 3. Strategies compared under the same constraints and scenarios
| Strategy | Bill | Artist fees | vs recommended | Disruption scenarios continued | Unchanged | Evidence coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Strongest cultural fit | Michael Kiwanuka + Sault | $13,500 | — | 27/27 | 15 | 75% |
| Lower-cost alternative · Most robust under disruption · Preferred without the city signal | Michael Kiwanuka + Jordan Rakei | $10,000 | −$3,500, −7.14 pts | 27/27 | 25 | 75% |
- **Strongest cultural fit:** Highest declared policy score among all feasible bills: the best-supported cultural fit under the declared model. Recommended: it maximizes the declared cultural-fit objective and continues in 27/27 disruption scenarios.
- **Lower-cost alternative · Most robust under disruption · Preferred without the city signal:** Best policy score among cheaper bills: saves $3,500 for 7.14 policy points. Continues in 27/27 disruption scenarios (25 unchanged) versus 27/27 (15 unchanged) for the recommendation. The optimizer's choice under a location-free Qloo ranking [a1]. Prefer it if the $3,500 saving matters more than the cultural-fit gap, or if the artist budget may fall below $13,500. Prefer it if cancellations, fee increases or budget cuts are likely: it gives up 7.14 policy points for that resilience. Prefer it if the audience is not mainly local to New York.
- Robustness definition: Budget cuts of 5, 10, 15 and 20%; +10, +20 and +30% on each bookable artist's fee; each bookable artist becoming unavailable; and three combined shocks (5% cut with all fees +10%, 10% with +15%, 15% with +20%). "Held": the planned bill stays feasible unchanged. "Repaired": one act is swapped and the others stay booked. "Failed": no bill keeps the other acts.

## 4. Backups if an act becomes unavailable
- Michael Kiwanuka: 1) Sault + Jordan Rakei ($10,500, 32.964286 pts); 2) Sault + Hiatus Kaiyote ($12,500, 17.053571 pts)
- Sault: 1) Michael Kiwanuka + Jordan Rakei ($10,000, 61.535714 pts); 2) Michael Kiwanuka + Hiatus Kaiyote ($12,000, 45.625 pts)

## 5. Fees and availability (assumptions, not verified facts)
| Artist | Fee | Fee status | Availability | Needs confirmation |
